To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DPCPLP protocol can be used in Adhoc networks to increase the battery power of nodes, increase the availability of links, and improve the throughput.
DPCPLP provides better throughput and link availability than AODV and AODV with optimum transmit power.
the DPCPLP approach provides better performance than the existing approaches in terms of packet delivery ratio, end-to-end delay, energy consumption and throughput.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a cross layer approach for power conservation and link prediction to increase network throughput in an Adhoc networks.
the design of a novel cross layer approach for link prediction in mobile adhoc networks.

the following objectives: (1) to propose a cross layer design for link prediction and power control in Adhoc networks; (2) to analyze the performance of the proposed method in terms of throughput, energy consumption and packet drops; (3) to compare the proposed method with the standard AODV protocol and (4) to compare the performance of the standard AODVs with and without link failure prediction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DPCPLP approach is better than AODV and the DPLP approach in terms of throughput and energy conservation.
the proposed method of cross layer interaction for power control and prediction of links in Adhoc network provides a combined solution of power conservation as well energy efficient routing.
the proposed cross layer design for DPCPLP is able to reduce the energy consumption and increase the link availability in an Adhoc networks.

the cross layer approach is used to predict link availability and power conservation for Adhoc networks.
the proposed DPCPLP method outperforms AODV routing and DPC methods in terms of packet drops, network throughput, battery life and network lifetime in an Adhoc scenario.
the DPCPLP method provides an effective solution for power control as well as link prediction for Adhoc networks.

the proposed DPCPLP approach outperforms the existing AODV protocol in the terms of throughput and packet loss rate.
